Every beat is one narration clip; art.at names the phrases a picture waits for, and the page refuses to load if a phrase is not in its beat's say. The chapters follow LESSON['lecture'] in content/lesson-7.py part by part (light sources; shining back; darkness; a model of light; how ideas changed), in the lesson's own words and examples: the Sun, lamp, candle, torch and fire of its explore step; the Moon, mirror and white paper of its sort, its dark cupboard test and its two bins; its dark room (ART.sim darkRoom: curtains, lamp) with its three predictions; its model of light (the RAY_MODEL drawing, straight lines from the source to the eye) and its globe (ART.scene globe); and the eyes that were once thought to send out beams. People are brown (renderer.skin).
title: Light and Dark
subtitle: Grade 2 Science
objectives: Know that there are many light sources, including the Sun.
Know that darkness is the absence of light.
Sort and group objects, materials and living things based on observations of the similarities and differences between them.
Make predictions about what they think will happen.
Describe what happened during an enquiry and if it matched their predictions.
Know that a model represents an object or idea in a clear way.
Talk about how some of the scientific knowledge and thinking now was different in the past.

beats.say: Light lets you see. It comes from a light source, like the Sun.
Take all the light away, and it is dark. Dark is no light at all.
The Sun, a lamp, a candle, a torch, a fire.
Each one makes its own light. Each one is a light source.
Switch it off, or blow it out, and the light stops.
The Sun is the biggest light source we have. Daylight is sunlight.
The Moon is bright at night. Is it a light source?
No. It makes no light of its own. It shines back the Sun's light.
A mirror and white paper shine light back too.
Put them in a dark cupboard, and they go dark. So they are not sources.
Now sort them into two groups: makes light, or only shines it back.
Here is a room. Daylight comes in, and the lamp is on.
Predict: with the curtains shut and the lamp off, what will you see?
Close the curtains. The lamp still lights the room.
Now switch off the lamp. It is completely dark.
You cannot see anything, because there is no light to see by.
Did that match your prediction? Switch the lamp on, and you can see again.
Darkness is what is left when there is no light.
We cannot see light travelling. So scientists draw a model of it.
They draw light as straight lines, from the source to your eye.
That drawing is a model: a clear way of showing an idea.
A globe is a model of the Earth. It shows the shape and the seas.
It leaves out every house and tree. A model leaves the rest out.
Long ago, some people thought eyes sent out beams, like torches.
If that were true, you could see in a dark room. You cannot.
Testing showed that light comes from a source, into your eye.
What people know changes when they test it.
A light source makes its own light. The Sun is the biggest one.
The Moon, a mirror and white paper only shine light back.
Darkness is not a thing. It is what is left when there is no light.
A model shows an idea clearly. Ideas change when people test them.
